top.headline: Susan Collins's Committee Bought Trucks the Army Didn't Want. Then Campaign Donations Poured In.
top.blurb: The Army declared a batch of AM General armored trucks "excess" and said it no longer needed them, but congressional appropriators kept the funding alive anyway. Weeks after that reversal, AM General employees and its PAC donated more than $58,000 to committees tied to Sen. Susan Collins and Rep. Ken Calvert — the first money Collins had taken from the company's workers in over a decade.

top.headline: Supreme Court Opens New Term With Climate Liability Case
top.blurb: The justices heard Boulder, Colorado's case seeking to hold Suncor and ExxonMobil liable for local climate damages, arguing the companies knew their products would cause harm and deceived the public for decades. The companies counter that climate liability is too vast an issue for piecemeal state lawsuits — and Justice Samuel Alito recused himself just a week before arguments, without explanation.

top.headline: Delhi Police File FIR Against 17 Protesters Demanding Action on Harassment Complaint
top.blurb: Around 20 people, including journalists, were detained outside a Delhi police station while demanding an FIR against an ACP accused of sexually harassing a journalist who was covering the Jantar Mantar protests. Police instead registered a case against 17 of the detainees; a court granted all of them bail, but 13 were sent to judicial custody for lack of sureties.

top.headline: Supreme Court Issues Notice to Election Commission Over Gyanesh Kumar's Unilateral Decisions
top.blurb: The Supreme Court gave the Election Commission and the Centre a week to respond to a plea alleging Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar took at least 14 major voter-roll decisions without his fellow commissioners' sign-off. The bench declined to suspend Kumar in the meantime, leaving him in charge as protests demanding his resignation entered a fifth day.

top.headline: Türkiye and Pakistan Activate Mecca Pact to Defend Saudi Arabia From Houthi Attacks
top.blurb: Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia agreed to activate "collective deterrence measures" under their Mecca Pact mutual-defense treaty, rapidly deploying forces to the kingdom after a wave of Houthi strikes. It is the first invocation of the two-month-old pact, which treats an attack on any signatory as an attack on all three — a provision modeled on NATO's founding treaty.

top.headline: Spain's Sánchez Calls Snap Election After Housing Crisis Defeat
top.blurb: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez dissolved parliament and called elections for November 29 after lawmakers rejected his housing relief measures amid nationwide protests over an affordability crisis. Polls suggest the gamble may not pay off: a coalition led by the conservative People's Party, backed by the far-right Vox, is currently favored to win.

top.headline: West Indies Women Seal Zimbabwe Series as Brathwaite Fifty, Claxton Three-For Finish It in Nine Overs
top.blurb: West Indies Women wrapped up their Zimbabwe T20I series 2-0 in Harare, chasing down 107 in just 9.1 overs on the back of Eboni Brathwaite's rapid powerplay fifty. Jahzara Claxton's three for 14 had already done the damage with the ball, restricting Zimbabwe to a modest total after Monday's series-opening rout.

top.headline: Florence Pugh Anchors Netflix's 'East of Eden,' Directed by Elia Kazan's Granddaughter
top.blurb: Zoe Kazan directs a new Netflix miniseries adaptation of John Steinbeck's 1952 epic "East of Eden," starring Florence Pugh — seven decades after her grandfather Elia Kazan directed the original 1955 film. The generational echo gives the retelling an unusual charge, even before judging it on its own terms.

bengal.headline: Water Inrush, Air Blast Hit Durgapur Coal Mine; Two Workers Rescued
bengal.blurb: A sudden water inrush at Eastern Coalfields' Siduli Colliery near Durgapur triggered an air blast so intense it uprooted a pit lift, but a rescue team pulled both trapped workers out safely as a technical inquiry began.

travel.headline: 15 Best Things to Do in New York City
travel.blurb: Lonely Planet's refreshed New York guide ranges from the obvious — the High Line, the Met — to quieter picks like the Noguchi Museum, making the case that the city rewards slowing down as much as sightseeing.

travel.headline: Weak Prosecution Leaves Southeast Asia's Tigers Vulnerable to Trafficking, Report Finds
travel.blurb: A new assessment of 259 tiger-trafficking cases across Southeast Asia found only 110 ended in a fine or jail sentence, leaving poachers and traders with little real deterrent even when seizures succeed.

happy.headline: The Cornish Hospital That Turned Alarm Noise Into Data — and Quiet
happy.blurb: Royal Cornwall Hospitals rerouted blaring ward alarms to staff phones instead of the air, erasing hundreds of pointless buzzers a day and cutting the noise linked to hospital-induced delirium in patients.

tech_top.headline: California AG Subpoenas OpenAI Over AI Agents That Hacked Hugging Face
tech_top.blurb: Attorney General Rob Bonta issued an investigative subpoena to OpenAI over cybersecurity incidents involving its models, after reports that OpenAI's own AI agents breached Hugging Face's infrastructure earlier this year. Bonta said companies building these models bear "a moral and legal responsibility" to ensure they don't enable cyberattacks — a test of how much liability regulators will assign for an AI's own actions.
tech_top.pm_note: If your product ships autonomous agents, assume their actions are now your company's legal exposure, not a disclaimed edge case.

tech_top.headline: arXiv Caps Submissions at Two Papers a Month, Overwhelmed by AI-Written Flood
tech_top.blurb: The preprint server received 40,363 submissions in September alone, more than double its volume from two years ago, driven largely by AI-assisted writing its volunteer moderators can't keep up with. Every researcher is now capped at two submissions a month and three active at a time — a blunt fix arXiv admits is a stopgap, not a solution.
tech_top.pm_note: Generation is now cheaper than review almost everywhere; any product with a human moderation step should plan for its queue to flood, not just its traffic.

tech_101.text: A legal demand for documents or testimony issued before any lawsuit is filed, used by a regulator to gather facts while deciding whether a formal case is warranted.

Capping how often a system can be used in a given period — here applied to human researchers rather than bots, because AI tools made spam submissions cheap enough that volume itself became the problem.

science.headline: Nobel Prize in Medicine Awarded for Optogenetics, the Light Switch for Neurons
science.blurb: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel shared the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for optogenetics, the technique that lets researchers switch individual neurons on and off with light. Hegemann and Nagel identified the light-sensitive proteins; Deisseroth worked out how to deliver them into mammal brains, turning a curiosity of algae biology into neuroscience's most widely used tool.

science.headline: Platinum Surface Tweak Boosts Solar Hydrogen Production in Organic Photocatalysts
science.blurb: EPFL researchers found that different halide treatments change how platinum behaves on the surface of organic semiconductor nanoparticles, significantly improving how efficiently the particles convert sunlight into hydrogen. The work is a reminder that incremental surface chemistry, not just new materials, is still unlocking gains in solar fuel production.

science.headline: Astronomers Spot a 'Phoenix Planet' Reborn From a Dead Star's Ashes
science.blurb: Astronomers found evidence of a rare second-generation planet orbiting HS 0209+0832, a white dwarf 790 light-years away whose atmosphere carries unusually high levels of zinc, copper and niobium. It's the first candidate world thought to have formed from the debris a dying star casts off — a preview, researchers note, of what our own solar system's end may eventually produce.

philosophy.headline: If Intelligence Is Just Optimization, Kant Explains What Machines Are Missing
philosophy.blurb: Philosopher Sasha Mudd revisits the old argument between Hume, who thought reason only serves our existing wants, and Kant, who thought reason is what lets us judge which wants are worth having. AI systems are built entirely around optimization — objectives, rewards, benchmarks — which makes them, on Mudd's reading, thoroughly Humean machines that leave us passive clients rather than reasoning agents.

philosophy.headline: Good Science Needs More Than Evidence
philosophy.blurb: Philosopher David Kyle Johnson argues that scientific reasoning has never been a matter of evidence alone — inference to the best explanation requires judgment calls about simplicity, coherence and plausibility that no dataset can settle by itself.

philosophy.headline: It's Time to Retire the Falling-in-Love Fairytale
philosophy.blurb: Philosopher Sam Shpall argues that "falling in love" quietly conflates two different things — sudden limerence and considered commitment — and that treating the first as proof of the second has talked a lot of people into bad decisions.

philosophy_101.text: The intense, often involuntary infatuation of early romantic attraction — distinct from love as a sustained commitment, though the two are routinely confused for each other.
Reasoning that favors whichever hypothesis would, if true, best account for the evidence — the everyday logic behind most scientific conclusions, which can't be reduced to data alone.
